title: Independence of the local Frobenius operator from the embedding
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ with
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, a Weil complex $K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$, a closed
point $y\in|Y_0|$ of degree $r=[\kappa(y):\Fq]$, and an integer $j\in\mathbf
Z$. For two $k_0$-embeddings $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ with associated geometric
points $\bar y,\bar y'\to Y$, the local operators $F_y$ and $F'_y$ on the
stalks of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)$
constructed in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] are conjugate: there is an
isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar y}\cong \mathcal
H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar y'}$ carrying $F_y$ to $F'_y$.

proof.text: The source-library lemmas FiniteField.exists_apply_eq_pow_card_pow_of_comp_eq and FiniteField.exists_geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_pow_apply_eq give a positive t such that gamma^t composed with iota equals iota'. Finiteness and the cardinality q^r of the residue field follow from the closed-point finite-field theorem and Module.natCard_eq_pow_finrank. Set emb_i=gamma^i composed with iota. Each emb_i is k_0-compatible because gamma is a k_0-algebra automorphism.

Set x_i=localClosedPoint(emb_i). Compare the two pullback projections using galoisMap_projections and contravariant Spec functoriality. The model projection gives gamma composed with emb_i=emb_(i+1); the closure projection is h on both sides. Thus x_(i+1)g=h x_i, with this direction for geometric powers. Each x_i has the prescribed residue-degree return by localClosedPoint_return.

Apply the one-step compatibility theorem to x_(i+1),x_i with n=r-1. Its explicitly constructed map a_i:C_i→C_(i+1) is an isomorphism and satisfies a_i F_(i+1)=F_i a_i in Lean composition order. Starting with the identity, inductively compose these a_i to construct e_i:C_0≅C_i satisfying e_i F_i=F_0 e_i. The induction step is associativity followed by the one-step equation and the previous intertwining equation.

Use emb_0=iota and emb_t=iota' to identify the two endpoint operators. Apply coefficientFdCohomology(E,j).mapIso to e_t. Functor.map_comp sends its intertwining equation to the required equality of the two closed-point cohomology operators. This works equally for zero cohomology.

The current main-20261015 statement is the same; its file has no proof text.

tool_uses.why: Only clause (a), finite residue extension at a closed point of a finite-type scheme, is used; the unit has no such field-theoretic tool.
Only clause (1), invertibility of point transport for every point complex, is used, instantiated with auxiliary Y_0=Spec k_0; no cohomological finiteness route is replaced.
Naturality of the specified rational point transport is needed to expand the stalk return; it is a generic functorial tool, not a replacement of a finiteness-unit step.
The natural associative composition comparisons, then rationalized, identify the specified point transports; this is generic pullback coherence.

lean.statement: theorem localFrobeniusConjugacyClass (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (c : D.CoefficientDatum) (E : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields c.l c.Qbar) (Y₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [LocallyOfFiniteType Y₀.hom] [QuasiCompact Y₀.hom] (K : sfWeilComplex D c.l c.different Y₀ E.val) (y : {y : Y₀.left // y ∈ closedPoints Y₀.left}) (ι ι' : Y₀.left.residueField y.val →+* D.k) (hι : ι.comp (Y₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap y.val) = algebraMap D.k₀ D.k) (hι' : ι'.comp (Y₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap y.val) = algebraMap D.k₀ D.k) (j : ℤ) : ∃ e : (DerivedCategory.coefficientFdCohomology E.val j).obj (localPointComplex c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K (localClosedPoint D Y₀ y ι hι)) ≅ (DerivedCategory.coefficientFdCohomology E.val j).obj (localPointComplex c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K (localClosedPoint D Y₀ y ι' hι')), e.hom ≫ (localClosedFrobeniusCohomology c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K y ι' hι' j) = (localClosedFrobeniusCohomology c.l E.val D c.different Y₀ K y ι hι j) ≫ e.hom

blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite
extension $E/\Ql$, $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$ with
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, a Weil complex $(K,\theta)$ with $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$ as in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], a closed
point $y\in|Y_0|$ of degree $r=[\kappa(y):\Fq]$, and an integer $j\in\mathbf
Z$. For two embeddings $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ with associated geometric
points $\bar y,\bar y'\to Y$, the local operators $F_y$ and $F'_y$ on the
stalks of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^j(K)$
constructed in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] are conjugate: there is an
isomorphism $\mathcal H^j(K)_{\bar y}\cong \mathcal
H^j(K)_{\bar y'}$ carrying $F_y$ to $F'_y$.

proof.text:
Two embeddings $\kappa(y)\hookrightarrow k$ differ by an element of
$\operatorname{Gal}(k/k_0)$, because $k$ is the fixed algebraic closure of the
finite field $k_0$ and $\kappa(y)$ is a finite field; the associated
geometric points $\bar y$ and $\bar y'$ of $Y$ are therefore related by a
power of the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $g_Y$ of
[def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. That automorphism induces an isomorphism between the
stalks of the cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^j(K)$ at the two
points, and the Weil isomorphism is an isomorphism
$\theta:Lg_Y^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ in $\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$, which
intertwines the local operator built at $\bar y$ with the one built at its
translate. Iterating this and using the $r$-fold return prescribed in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] transports $F_y$ to $F'_y$, which is the
conjugacy asserted.
